newsitem.title: UK: First by-election of UK parliament set for July 31.
newsitem.headline: First by-election of UK parliament set for July 31.

text.p: The first by-election of the new British parliament will take place on July 31, giving an early indication of how the popularity of the Labour Government under Tony Blair is holding up.
The writ for the by-election at Uxbridge on the western fringes of London was moved by the Conservative Party in the House of Commons on Wednesday.
Conservative Sir Michael Shersby held on in Uxbridge at the May 1 general election, repulsing a Labour challenge by just 724 votes, but died suddenly less than a week afterwards.

New Conservative leader William Hague will hope that John Randall, who was Shersby's election agent, will retain the seat, boosting his depleted House of Commons forces to 165. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
